Sector Snapshot: Investors Turn Up The Volume On Voice AI
Mary Ann Azevedo
November 18, 2026
Mary Ann Azevedo

Voice AI — technology that lets computers understand and generate human speech — is drawing billions of dollars from investors as startups find more ways to put it to work.
Companies developing or offering the technology have raised at least $9.5 billion in venture funding so far in 2026, according to Crunchbase data. The recipients range from companies building speech recognition and generation tools to those offering voice agents for customer service. Others use voice AI for creative work or accessibility, or build the infrastructure and chips that power the technology.
The broad trend: Investors are putting more money into fewer startups developing or offering voice AI technology and are backing everything from automated customer service to speech generation and content creation.
The funding surge also reflects the broader AI boom, with some of the largest rounds going to infrastructure and generative media companies whose businesses extend beyond voice. Multiple companies are raising rounds in quick succession.
The numbers: So far in 2026, startups developing or offering voice AI technology have raised $9.5 billion globally, Crunchbase data shows. As of Nov. 11, funding had already exceeded 2025 by 67%, with 154 reported deals versus 273 in 2025. Overall, deal volume is on track to fall for a second consecutive year — pointing to a market where investors are putting more money into fewer companies.
Unsurprisingly, given the AI boom, funding for the space has continued to climb in recent years compared to past levels, surging from $2.8 billion in 2021 to $5.7 billion in 2025.
Notable rounds
The largest rounds in Crunchbase’s voice AI micro-industry went well beyond speech synthesis, encompassing infrastructure, generative media and customer service agents.
The biggest individual financing went to Fireworks AI , which raised a $1.5 billion Series D in July at a $17.5 billion valuation. The San Mateo, California-based company is an AI infrastructure provider whose offerings include speech recognition. Atreides Management , Index Ventures and TCV co-led the round, with participation from investors including Nvidia and Lightspeed Venture Partners .
San Francisco-based Fal was the largest funding recipient across multiple rounds in 2026, raising $1.65 billion in total. That included a $1.3 billion Series F led by Bessemer Venture Partners , completed in October at a reported $16 billion valuation, doubling its valuation from its $350 million Sequoia Capital -led financing in April. The company provides infrastructure for running image, video and audio models.
Customer service AI also attracted substantial investment. San Francisco-based Sierra raised $950 million in May, led by Tiger Global and GV , at a reported $15.8 billion valuation. Its platform lets businesses deploy agents across voice, chat and other customer channels.
Meanwhile, Amsterdam-based Wonderful raised a $550 million Series C in September, led by Insight Partners , at a $5 billion valuation. That followed a $150 million Series B in March, bringing its total 2026 funding to $700 million as it expanded from conversational agents into broader enterprise automation.
Among companies focused on AI-generated speech, New York-based ElevenLabs announced a $500 million Series D in February, led by Sequoia Capital, at an $11 billion valuation. That was more than triple its valuation a year earlier. Additional institutional and strategic investors joined in later tranches, bringing the Series D total to $561 million. ElevenLabs allows creators, enterprises and others to use AI software to replicate voices in dozens of languages. The company is investing in conversational agents, expressive speech and dubbing.
Beijing-based ModelBest , which develops compact AI models that run on devices, also ranks among the largest recipients of funding this year, with a $591 million Series C in July.
Exits
Voice AI companies have also begun delivering exits. In January, Deepgram acquired OfOne , which automates restaurant and drive-thru orders.
In September, Inworld acquired Ultravox , a developer of conversational voice AI technology.
The sector also saw an IPO. Neosapience , the South Korean company behind synthetic voice platform Typecast, listed on the KOSDAQ on Sept. 21.
Looking ahead, additional acquisitions are in the pipeline. Automation Anywhere agreed to acquire Boost.ai , an enterprise voice and chat AI provider, in October. And Deepgram announced plans to acquire Daily , creator of the Pipecat voice-agent framework.
More recently, Five9 agreed to acquire Level AI for $325 million in cash, adding technology that analyzes customer conversations, assists contact-center workers and automates voice and digital interactions. The Level AI transaction is expected to close by year’s end.
Overall, the space is booming, and it doesn’t look like interest in voice AI will die anytime soon. Tom Hulme , managing partner and head of Europe at GV, told Crunchbase News in 2025 that one of the most exciting trends he believes is underway in the growth of voice AI is that “we’re returning to humanity’s most natural form of communication.”
After decades of adapting ourselves to technology, “technology is finally adapting to us,” he said.

MEIL Group raises $700 million from global investors, valued at ₹1 trillion
MEIL Group has raised around $700 million through structured equity and proposed road asset monetisation, with funds reportedly linked to a family stake acquisition deal
Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Limited (Photo: MEIL website) Shine Jacob Chennai
3 min read Last Updated : Nov 18 2026 | 6:34 PM IST
Listen to This Article
Hyderabad-based Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Limited (MEIL) Group has raised approximately $700 million through an innovative financing structure involving structured equity and the proposed monetisation of its road assets, according to sources familiar with the development.
Three of the world’s leading global investment firms — DK, HH and Värde Partners — participated in the transaction, demonstrating their confidence in the group’s vision, diversified business interests and long-term growth prospects.
This is reportedly part of a family settlement between MEIL Managing Director P V Krishna Reddy and his uncle, Pamireddy Pitchi Reddy, founder and executive chairman of the company. Krishna Reddy has raised this money as part of the plan to finance the acquisition of his uncle P P Reddy's stake in the company.
According to sources, investors have recognised MEIL Group as a strong platform to participate in India’s next decade of infrastructure expansion and economic growth. Their decision to partner with the group reflects confidence in its ambitious vision, diversified presence across key sectors and one of the strongest project execution capabilities in the industry.
The confidence of global investors is also reflected in the valuations assigned to the businesses. MEIL has been valued at approximately ₹1 trillion, while EPTL, the group’s energy transition business, has been valued at around ₹14,000 crore at this stage. These valuations underline the scale of the group’s operations and the significant potential of its businesses.

“Global investors see MEIL Group as an opportunity to participate in India’s long-term infrastructure and growth story. Their participation reflects confidence in the group’s vision, diversified business portfolio and proven execution capabilities. It is a strong endorsement of the group’s growth journey and future ambitions,” a source familiar with the development said.
Over the past three decades, MEIL has grown into one of India’s prominent infrastructure and engineering groups, with projects across more than 20 countries. Its diversified portfolio spans irrigation, transportation, energy, oil and gas, manufacturing, clean mobility and advanced infrastructure.
The group’s portfolio includes several landmark national infrastructure projects, including the Zojila Tunnel, Mumbai Coastal Road, Thane-Borivali Twin Tunnel, Polavaram Project, Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Scheme and Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Project. Its road projects extend across approximately 1,975 kilometres.
Reports of the uncle-nephew duo reaching a family settlement first became public in June last year.
In the energy sector, MEIL’s capabilities span hydrocarbons, power generation, renewable energy and energy storage. The group is developing pumped storage projects with a combined capacity exceeding 9,110 megawatts (MW) and implementing approximately 3,000 MW of solar power projects. Its entry into India’s nuclear energy programme through the construction of two 700 MWe reactors at Kaiga further strengthens its presence in strategic infrastructure.
The group’s international operations include major packages in Mongolia’s first greenfield oil refinery, while its domestic portfolio covers critical energy infrastructure and refinery projects.
Beyond conventional infrastructure, the group is expanding its presence in emerging sectors through its businesses and subsidiaries. Olectra and EveyTrans are advancing electric mobility, while Drillmec and ICOMM strengthen its global capabilities in drilling technology, manufacturing, telecommunications and strategic infrastructure. Megha Gas continues to expand its city gas distribution network across multiple states.
The group’s initiatives in healthcare, skill development and community development further reflect its commitment to nation-building.
"The $700 million transaction represents a major milestone in MEIL Group’s growth journey, highlighting the confidence of leading global investors in its vision, capabilities and future potential. It also reinforces the group’s ambition to play a defining role in India’s infrastructure and economic transformation," said a source.

candidates.snippet: Jay-Z-Backed Music Financing Startup Duetti Raises $665M AfroTech
candidates.text:
A Jay-Z-backed music financing startup has raised new funding.
Duetti, founded it in 2022, provides capital, marketing, and catalog management services to artists, songwriters, and producers, according to its website. The company has completed more than 1,600 catalog deals and now owns music catalogs spanning over 50,000 master recordings and compositions, representing more than 3,000 artists, a press release mentioned.
Christopher Nolte, a former Apple Music business development executive, and Lior Tibon, who previously served as chief operating officer of TIDAL, founded Duetti. TIDAL is an ad-free music streaming subscription service, according to Variety, that Jay-Z once held a majority stake in until he sold it to Block in 2021 for $350 million, Fox Business reports.
Duetti has raised more than $1.3 billion as of this writing. The total includes a $32 million funding round in 2023, with Viola Ventures and Viola Credit, Untitled Presight Capital, and Jay-Z’s Roc Nation participating, Music Business Worldwide reports.
Duetti announced its most recent funding round on Nov. 17, 2026. According to the press release, the company raised $665 million. Carlyle’s Asset-Backed Finance (ABF) team, part of its Global Credit platform, led the round with a $450 million investment. Viola Credit, Flexpoint Ford, and Truist Bank also supported the raise. The funding will help Duetti expand across genres and geographic markets and pursue additional music rights opportunities.
“This funding marks a significant milestone for Duetti, firmly placing us among a distinguished group of music rights platforms operating at real scale, which allows us to unlock substantial benefits in terms of market intelligence and operating capabilities,” Tibon (CEO) said in the press release. “Our third ABS transaction in just two years is more than five times the size of our inaugural deal in 2024, demonstrating our rapid growth, strong track record, and increasing institutional demand for our catalog and business model.”
Akhil Bansal, Carlyle’s head of asset-backed finance, commented:
“We anchored this securitization because independent music royalties can generate the kind of recurring, diversified cash flows that asset-backed finance is built around. Duetti pairs real industry expertise with the data and technology to build and manage catalogs at scale, and that’s what gives us conviction in the platform.”

New funding follows a year in which Jeeves' total platform volume and revenue grew more than 3x YoY. The company also named Alexander Melikian President and Chief Financial Officer.
MIAMI , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Jeeves, the global financial operating system for enterprises that operate in multiple countries, today announced new funding from Neuberger Berman Specialty Finance, bringing financing capacity to $300 million. The capital supports the continued growth of Jeeves' corporate card, spend management, and payments platform, which now processes more than $5 billion in annualized volume for thousands of enterprises across 35 countries.
This financing is incremental to the company's $110 million equity round announced in September, led by CoinFund with participation from AllianceBernstein, Andreessen Horowitz, Coinbase Ventures, CRV, FJ Labs, GIC, Global PayTech Ventures, ParaFi Ventures, Vista, Wintermute Ventures, Y Combinator and others. Together, these back to back fund raises enable Jeeves to save its customers time and money, from automation of financial workflows with corporate cards to managing corporate treasury with multi-currency balances.
The financing follows strong momentum in Jeeves' core business, with total platform volume up 3.4x YoY, and stablecoin -settled activity growing from zero to more than $2 billion annualized volume in nine months. Thousands of businesses in sectors such as technology, mobility, financial services, retail and e-commerce, including industry leaders like BMW, H&M, Lululemon, Burger King, Kavak and XP run their global operations on Jeeves. Jeeves provides global enterprises corporate cards, accounts payable and treasury payments, spend management and agentic workflows, on a single piece of infrastructure running on stablecoin rails.
"Global enterprises want one platform to hold, move, and manage money in every market they operate in, and a real banking platform has to be able to extend capital to its customers as easily as it automates a workflow," said Alexander Melikian, President and Chief Financial Officer of Jeeves . "Neuberger is one of the most respected specialty finance investors in the world, and their partnership is a strong endorsement of the quality of our platform, the strength of our enterprise customer base, and the discipline with which we have built it."
"Jeeves has built a modern banking platform designed to address the evolving needs of global enterprises underserved by legacy financial infrastructure," said Peter Sterling, Managing Director and Head of Specialty Finance at Neuberger. "We were impressed by the quality of the platform, the strength of the team and the performance of the business, and we look forward to supporting its continued growth."
Alexander Melikian Named President and Chief Financial Officer
Jeeves also announced that Alexander Melikian has been named President and Chief Financial Officer, effective immediately. Melikian joined Jeeves in 2022 as Chief Financial Officer and has scaled the company's finance, capital markets, treasury, and risk functions. In that time he has led more than $500 million in equity and debt financings, established the funding structures that support the platform's growth, and guided Jeeves' expansion into providing financial services across 35 markets around the world.
"Alex has been a driving force behind Jeeves' growth since the day he joined and the architect of the balance sheet that makes our platform possible," said Dileep Thazhmon, Founder and CEO of Jeeves . "He already operates as a partner across every part of the company. Naming him President recognizes that, and gives us the leadership structure to execute on the opportunity in front of us."
Prior to Jeeves, Melikian spent nearly a decade at Payoneer, the global B2B payments platform, where he led finance, corporate strategy, and corporate development and led the company's 2021 listing on Nasdaq. He previously held M&A advisory roles at PwC and corporate finance roles at Comcast NBCUniversal. He holds a Master of Accounting and a B.S. in Management in Finance and Business Legal Studies from Tulane University.

About Jeeves
Jeeves is the global financial operating system for enterprises that do business in multiple countries. Jeeves gives businesses physical and virtual corporate cards, accounts payable and treasury payments, and a spend management platform on a single piece of infrastructure, running on stablecoin rails that settle in minutes instead of days. AI agents handle reconciliation and financial automation, and accounts receivable and other financial workflows run on the same foundation. Thousands of enterprises worldwide, including BMW, H&M, Lululemon, Burger King, XP, and Kavak, use Jeeves to move billions of dollars a year.
About Neuberger Private Markets
Neuberger Private Markets is a division of Neuberger and has been an active and successful private markets investor since 1987. Neuberger Private Markets invests across strategies, asset classes, and geographies for a large number of sophisticated and renowned institutions and individuals globally. As of June 30, 2026, Neuberger Private Markets manages over $170 billion of investor commitments across primaries, co-investments, secondaries, private credit, and specialty strategies. Neuberger Private Markets has an experienced and diverse team of over 500 professionals with a global presence in 11 countries globally.

Spend management platform Payhawk announces $280M raise, 2B valuation
U.K.-based fintech Payhawk announced a $280 million Series C funding round Wednesday, led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm, making it one of Europe’s largest Series C rounds this year, as noted by Sifted . The round values the company at $2 billion, bringing its total funding to more than $500 million to date.
Founded in 2018, Payhawk is an enterprise financial management platform that helps companies track and manage expenses and procurement using AI agents. Speaking to FinTech magazine , Payhawk’s co-founder and CEO, Hristo Borisov, said the company saw “an incredible growth opportunity and room to bring finance teams AI-native products that combine agents, payment infrastructure, and enterprise controls.”
Payhawk competes with spend management companies Pleo, Moss, and Spendesk, and says it operates in 33 countries. Notably, the company said it still has 70% of the $100 million it raised in 2022, a round that valued the company at $1 billion. This fresh capital will support its global expansion. Other investors in the round include Greenoaks, Lightspeed, and QED.

NEW YORK , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hone Health , a physician-led longevity platform that helps people design a personalized plan for their health and longevity, today announced it has raised $228M in financing. The round was led by MarcyPen Capital Partners , a first-of-its-kind global investment platform that provides strategic capital to growth stage consumer businesses that create, move, and lead culture. MarcyPen has been a partner to Hone for over two years, having led the company's Series A financing, a role that had not previously been disclosed, and continuing to support the company through follow-on investments.

The investment is structured as $28M in equity as a Series A financing and $200M in growth financing from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund (CVF).
David Grutman has joined Hone Health as a strategic investor and advisor. Grutman has also brought a group of high-profile strategic investors, including Marcello Hernández, Nick Jonas, Joe Jonas, Kevin Jonas, Braxton Berrios, and Kelly Rowland, Jason Strauss and Noah Tepperberg. Additional investors include former NBA player Josh Childress, along with Quentin Dolan, Raj Gokal, Tushar Jain, Kyle Samani, Halle Tecco, and Zachary Gordan. The financing brings Hone's total equity funding to $65 million. "Today, consumers have almost limitless options when it comes to preventative health, but what people are looking for is the highest level of insight into their metrics, so that they can make more informed decisions about their health," said Saad Alam, Co-Founder & CEO of Hone Health. "Hone combines comprehensive diagnostic testing, physician-led care, and AI-powered insights to deliver that level of understanding. This funding will allow us to extend that vision across new therapeutic categories and start building toward our ultimate vision: a research platform to accelerate health outcomes."

Broader Clinical Care: Launch and scale physician-led programs across metabolic health, PMOS, inflammation, and immunity, giving patients a more connected view of the factors influencing their health.
Advanced Diagnostics: Integrate additional diagnostic tools into longitudinal patient care, including full-body MRI, DEXA scans, coronary CT angiography, and gut microbiome analysis, while creating one of the most complete health datasets ever assembled.
Clinical Technology: Advance AI-enabled care and the tools that bring together lab results, health history, symptoms, medications, and longitudinal outcomes to help physicians personalize and adapt care – accelerating the buildout of the technology that turns biomarkers into personalized treatment plans.
Emerging Therapies: Launch a physician-supervised peptide program providing eligible patients with access to select peptide therapies where legally available and clinically appropriate.
Research & Trials: Accelerate the clinical trials infrastructure that allows Hone to understand what kinds of care are driving the best patient outcomes.
Introducing Hone Black
Finally, Hone will publicly launch Hone Black , its most comprehensive and personalized membership. The concierge longevity program has operated in stealth for the past year, serving a select group of high-profile patients.
Hone Black combines extensive diagnostics (1,600+ health markers) with ongoing medical care from a dedicated team of physicians responsible for whole-body care. Treatment options span prescription medications, supplements, peptides, and lifestyle guidance, as well as exosome and stem cell therapies.

Helical Fusion Receives Up To $126 Million From Japanese Government
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:31 AM
Helical Fusion Receives Up To $126 Million From Japanese Government
Helical Fusion has been selected for a Japanese government grant program providing a maximum subsidy of approximately ¥19.2 billion, or $126 million, to advance commercially viable fusion power. Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry administers the program, which is scheduled to continue through February 2029.
Including the new award, Helical Fusion’s cumulative funding and financing commitments total approximately ¥33.2 billion, or $218 million.
The company will use the support to accelerate an integrated demonstration device, design its first planned fusion power plant, and develop critical components.
Helix HARUKA Will Demonstrate Integrated Technologies
Helical Fusion is manufacturing and assembling Helix HARUKA at the National Institute for Fusion Science campus in Toki, Japan.
Assembly of one helical coil is nearly complete.
The first phase will include energization testing of high-temperature superconducting coils in 2027.
During a planned second phase in the early 2030s, the company intends to demonstrate the integrated operation of superconducting coils, blanket systems, and other essential technologies.
The program is designed to identify engineering and integration risks before construction of a commercial plant.
Helix KANATA Advances In Parallel
Helical Fusion will simultaneously conduct the basic engineering design for Helix KANATA, its first planned power plant.
The company does not intend to wait for every demonstration test to finish before beginning plant design. Instead, it will incorporate findings from HARUKA as they become available.
Its commercial strategy emphasizes three requirements—net electricity production, continuous operation, and maintainability.
Helical Fusion selected the stellarator configuration because it believes the approach can support all three requirements.
The technology draws upon approximately 70 years of Japanese fusion research. The National Institute for Fusion Science’s Large Helical Device has maintained plasma operation for 3,268 seconds.
Helical Fusion is coordinating work among approximately 40 Japanese companies specializing in electrical equipment, machinery, advanced materials, precision manufacturing, and plant engineering.
Commercial fusion remains technically challenging, and the company’s 2030s objective depends on successful engineering, financing, regulatory approval, construction, and testing.
KEY QUOTES:
We founded Helical Fusion with a clear conviction: fusion must become a reliable, commercially viable source of electricity. We chose the Helical Stellarator because we believe it offers the strongest pathway to achieving that goal.
Our progress stands on decades of scientific research and the commitment of partners who believed in our approach early on, investing their resources and engineering expertise to turn our plans into actual hardware.
We see this selection as recognition of the strength of our development plan for practical fusion power and the capabilities we have built to execute it. We are grateful for this substantial public investment and fully recognize the responsibility that comes with it. We will demonstrate its value through measurable engineering progress.
Our responsibility is to bring Japan’s decades of fusion research and manufacturing expertise together in a power plant that can reliably supply electricity. We are determined to lead that effort from Japan, working with partners.
With this support, we will accelerate the integrated demonstration of Helix HARUKA and the development of Helix KANATA, bringing us closer to commercially viable fusion power.
Takaya Taguchi, Co-Founder and CEO of Helical Fusion

Variational, a digital-asset derivatives trading protocol emerging as a leading challenger to Hyperliquid, has raised $110 million in new funding. The round valued the company at $1.5 billion, elevating it to unicorn status.
Bloomberg reported on Nov. 18 that Variational raised the money in a round led by Bain Capital Crypto, Bain Capital’s digital-asset investment arm. Bloomberg described it as a sizable deal at a time when fundraising across the broader digital-asset industry has slowed. Global venture capital firms including Dragonfly, HSG, Peak XV and 50T Fund also participated in the Series B round.
The company’s fundraising pace has been brisk. Variational raised $10.3 million in a seed round in October 2024 and $50 million in a Series A round led by Dragonfly in May. Just six months after that Series A, it secured funding equal to about 1.8 times the combined total of its previous two rounds, pushing cumulative capital raised to more than $170 million. Bain Capital Crypto and Dragonfly, both backers in the Series A, also joined the latest financing.
Rapid growth helped underpin the raise. Variational said its trading platform Omni has surpassed $475 billion in cumulative volume, $1.3 billion in open interest and 100,000 accounts since launching in early 2025. When the company announced its Series A in May, Omni had reported $200 billion in cumulative volume, $750 million in open interest and 50,000 accounts. That implies trading volume has increased about 2.4 times and the number of accounts has roughly doubled in six months.
Its market presence is expanding quickly as well. Citing DeFiLlama data, Bankless said Omni’s 30-day trading volume climbed to about $66.4 billion on Nov. 12 from $34 billion on Sept. 10, nearly doubling in two months. The platform ranked third in daily volume among perpetual futures exchanges, behind Hyperliquid and Lighter. Most of that performance came during a private beta period, when users generally needed an invite code to join. Omni ended the beta this month and fully opened to the public.
Omni supports leveraged trading across more than 550 digital assets and traditional financial markets. More than half of its daily trading volume now comes from traditional markets such as stocks, indexes and commodities. A key driver has been its swaps product, launched in September. The product connects liquidity from traditional financial institutions to on-chain traders, and volume topped $80 billion in just over two months. Hyperliquid and Lighter do not currently offer it. Variational said DeFiLlama data show Omni ranks among the top platforms by volume for trading traditional assets on-chain.
A differentiated business model is also one of its strengths. Omni uses its own liquidity providers, or OLPs, to source liquidity from digital-asset exchanges and traditional financial institutions and provide quotes. Unlike conventional on-chain exchanges that must build new order books and liquidity market by market, Omni taps liquidity already present in traditional and on-chain markets. It does not charge trading fees, instead generating revenue from bid-ask spreads. Bankless said research firm Alea Research estimated Variational’s third-quarter spread at 2.35 basis points as a share of trading volume. That is lower than Hyperliquid’s average perpetual futures fee of 2.40 basis points. Company data cited by Bloomberg showed annualized net revenue of $75 million based on results from August through November.
Investors have also given the company positive marks. Stefan Cohen, a partner at Bain Capital Crypto, said Variational is among the first teams to bring traditional derivatives liquidity directly on-chain. He added that the company combines the strengths of traditional trading venues — hundreds of markets, fee-free trading and deep liquidity — with blockchain transparency and faster settlement. Variational is led by executives with backgrounds at Google, Meta, Virtu, IMC and Jane Street.
Lucas Schuermann, Variational’s chief executive officer, told Bloomberg the company is ultimately targeting traditional brokerages such as Robinhood and Interactive Brokers. He acknowledged that Variational competes with Hyperliquid, but said the two platforms can coexist because Variational is building a very different type of product for traditional finance. He added that the swaps product is validating his view that replicating traditional market execution quality on-chain requires drawing liquidity from places where it already exists.

candidates.text:
Trinity Capital Provides $100 Million In Debt Financing To Phononic
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:20 AM
Trinity Capital Provides $100 Million In Debt Financing To Phononic
Trinity Capital has committed $100 million in debt financing to Phononic, supporting an expansion of the company’s manufacturing capacity for solid-state cooling systems used in artificial intelligence data centers.
Phononic is a North Carolina-based developer of software-defined thermal-control technology. The company plans to use the financing to increase production and meet growing customer demand as AI infrastructure operators look for new ways to cool high-performance computing equipment.
The financing comes as Phononic enters its next growth phase as a profitable company backed by venture and growth-equity investors.
Cooling AI Infrastructure At The Component Level
AI servers generate substantial heat because they rely on dense collections of high-performance processors, memory systems, networking equipment, and optical components.
If those components exceed their designed operating temperatures, systems can reduce performance through thermal throttling. Cooling requirements can also constrain the amount of computing equipment that data-center operators can install within an existing facility.
Phononic develops compact thermoelectric devices that provide cooling near the point where heat is generated. Its Thermal Control Systems combine solid-state cooling hardware with intelligent software controls.
The technology is designed for components including graphics processing units, high-bandwidth memory, networking silicon, and optical transceivers. Optical transceivers move information between computing systems and can become increasingly sensitive to heat as network speeds and equipment density increase.
Phononic’s Thermal Fabric software monitors conditions across a data-center environment and adjusts thermal control in response to changes in AI workloads. This workload-responsive approach is intended to deliver cooling where and when it is required instead of operating every component at a constant level.
The company says its technology can help infrastructure operators increase computing and facility capacity while reducing energy and water consumption. These are company claims, and actual outcomes will depend on the equipment, workloads, facilities, and deployment configuration involved.
Manufacturing Expansion Supports Customer Demand
Phononic’s systems are deployed with major U.S. hyperscale computing companies. The new debt capital will help the company expand manufacturing so it can deliver additional equipment as those customers build out AI infrastructure.
Debt financing can provide a growth-stage company with capital while avoiding the immediate ownership dilution associated with issuing additional equity. The borrower must still satisfy repayment and other contractual obligations established by the financing agreement.
Trinity Capital provides private credit across technology, equipment finance, healthcare and life sciences, sponsor finance, and asset-based lending. Since its founding in 2008, the firm has deployed more than $6.8 billion across over 511 investments as of September 30, 2026.
The transaction reflects growing investment in technologies designed to address the power, cooling, and networking requirements of AI computing. While much of the industry’s attention has centered on processors, thermal management is increasingly important to maintaining the performance and reliability of those systems.
Phononic is positioning its combination of hardware and software as a way to address thermal limits at the component level rather than relying exclusively on building-level cooling infrastructure.
KEY QUOTES:
As AI hardware continues to evolve, we believe precise, real-time cooling at the chip level is becoming increasingly important. Phononic has built the thermoelectric technology and software to address that need, and we’re pleased to back their team as demand for their solutions continues to build.
Phil Gager, Senior Managing Director of Tech Lending at Trinity Capital
AI infrastructure is advancing at an unprecedented pace, and cooling has become a critical bottleneck to growth, limiting both facility capacity and compute and optical performance. Our customers are demanding disruptive thermal control solutions that can overcome these limitations at scale. Our partnership with Trinity Capital enables us to accelerate manufacturing capacity expansion to meet that demand and support the next wave of growth across AI infrastructure.
Dr. Tony Atti, Founder and CEO of Phononic

candidates.snippet: ‘The Romans are laughing at us’: physical AI founder raises $97 million in quest to stop wasting time with archaic infrastructure maintenance Fortune
candidates.text:
Alex Hawkinson keeps a collection of Roman artifacts at BrightAI’s robot demo center, and he has a saying to go with them: “The Romans are laughing at us.”
Recommended Video
Think of the way the Romans inspected their roads, Hawkinson told Fortune : “They sent teams of technicians out periodically on schedule” to check on their infrastructure. Two thousand years later, power companies, water utilities, and pipeline operators still do. In his telling, two out of three of those trips turn up nothing to fix, and the failures that matter happen in between visits anyway.
Hawkinson is convinced this can change, and investors are paying for the idea. BrightAI said Wednesday it has raised $97 million in a round led by Smith Point Capital , the growth-stage firm started by former Salesforce co-CEO Keith Block. GE Vernova, already a BrightAI customer, also invested, along with Cobalt Capital, Marlinspike Partners, Zero Infinity Partners as well as existing backers Khosla Ventures, Inspired Capital, and Upfront Ventures. The round brings total funding to $184 million and values BrightAI at $750 million, according to a person familiar with the matter. Hawkinson insisted he “doesn’t care” about so-called unicorn status: The point is bring infrastructure out of the ancient Roman era.
His pitch has three parts. Replace scheduled human inspections with sensors and AI that watch infrastructure all the time. Go after what BrightAI estimates is more than $7 trillion a year in waste worldwide. And along the way, create a kind of data that has never existed: a continuous record of how pipes, poles, and pumps actually wear out. If it works, the companies running the world’s power and water get to stop paying for trips that find nothing.
The Roman method
The Romans knew the problem well. Frontinus, who was named Rome’s water commissioner by the emperor Nerva in the late first century A.D., wrote a treatise on running the city’s aqueducts. He worried about leaks in underground channels that were hard to find and fix, about people tapping the lines without permission, and about trees whose roots could damage the masonry.
BrightAI’s release says the systems that power modern life “still operate on a centuries-old model: inspect, detect, and react.” Hawkinson is a believer from personal experience. In 2011, the power went out at his family’s cabin in Leadville, Colo., a remote mountain town, and nobody knew until the pipes had frozen and burst and water had run through the walls. He built a connected sensor hub in his garage, launched it on Kickstarter as SmartThings, and sold the company to Samsung in 2014. He has cofounded eight companies and run four as CEO, all of which exited. He bootstrapped BrightAI, founded in 2019, for its first four years.
He spent the first half of his career in software as a service, and his SmartThings put sensors in people’s homes, not substations or sewers.
“I wasn’t from infrastructure,” he said. When he started going out in the field, at one point in a hard hat in a sewer, he was “shocked” by how the systems everyone depends on are actually monitored and break down. In industry after industry, he asked frontline technicians how often they get sent out and find nothing to fix. The answer kept coming back at 50% to 70% of the time. BrightAI’s release puts it more conservatively, at more than half of scheduled inspections.
He assumed at first the operators were doing it wrong. He came to see it as an equilibrium. Send crews less often, and something breaks catastrophically, so you send them more often. Send them more often, and the labor, which is expensive and often dangerous, becomes unaffordable. Operators settle where “two out of every three times they send somebody out, even the most talented operators, it’s unnecessary,” he said, and failures still slip through between visits.
The wooden power pole is his favorite example. By his count, the U.S. has about 150 million of them, “little matchsticks sticking up,” and each one sees a human inspector roughly every eight to 10 years. The 2018 Camp Fire—California’s deadliest wildfire—killed 85 people after a worn hook on an aging PG&E transmission tower gave way. Cal Fire determined the utility’s lines caused it. Hawkinson’s point is that the hook was “completely invisible in the world” until it failed.
$7 trillion of waste
The $7 trillion figure is BrightAI’s own. The company says it surveyed 12,158 operators across 16 industries and put the addressable annual impact at more than $7.5 trillion. It also found 98% of those operators lack adequate visibility into their assets. It tallies the wasted trips, the labor, and the cost of letting things break, which he said is far more expensive to fix than to maintain. The outside research the release cites—from the Energy Department, the EPA, Swiss Re and the National Safety Council—puts the cost of infrastructure failure alone at $2.5 trillion a year.
The examples Hawkinson gives are mundane, which is part of his point. He cited one customer, a UK water utility that has about a thousand pumps and can’t tell which ones will be the next to fail. Its limited staff runs around “like chickens with their heads cut off” trying to catch them. When heavy rain hits, failed pumps send raw sewage into rivers.
Hawkinson said he’s a Lord of the Rings fan, and this breaks his heart, to see raw sewage being pumped into a landscape that looks “just like the Shire.” (This Fortune interviewer agreed, saying Hawkinson’s physical AI descriptions sound a bit like something Gandalf would get up to; Hawkinson laughed, but didn’t quite agree.)
Closer to home, a break in the Potomac Interceptor sewer line in January released an estimated 243 million gallons of untreated wastewater into the Potomac River, according to the Maryland Department of the Environment.

VINCUE Raises $93 Million To Expand Its AI-First Automotive Retail Platform
VINCUE has raised $93 million in growth capital to accelerate development and adoption of its artificial intelligence platform for automotive dealerships.
Wavecrest Growth Partners led the investment, with participation from existing investor FM Capital. VINCUE plans to use the funding to advance its product roadmap and significantly expand its go-to-market, dealer performance, and customer-support organizations.
The investment follows two consecutive years in which VINCUE said it achieved growth of nearly 100%. The company attributed that expansion partly to its vehicle acquisition and merchandising products as franchised dealerships increasingly emphasize used vehicles as an important source of profitability.
VINCUE was founded by Chris Hoke, Danny Zaslavsky, Brian Kellogg, and Jeff Rice as a mobile vehicle-appraisal application. It has since developed a broader platform covering the vehicle lifecycle from inventory planning and acquisition through pricing, management, merchandising, and sale.
Protos Rebuilds VINCUE Around AI
A central focus of the financing is Protos, VINCUE’s new AI-native technology foundation.
Rather than adding AI as a separate feature to an existing platform, VINCUE has rebuilt its technology with AI embedded in the underlying system. The company introduced Protos Intelligence to more than 550 dealers, partners, and automotive professionals at its sold-out UNLEASHED 2026 conference in Kansas City.
Dealers can type or speak questions about their inventory and receive responses in plain language. This is intended to make operational data more accessible while helping dealership employees make faster inventory decisions.
Protos includes Signal Appraisal, which predicts a vehicle’s potential retail sale price. The model recalculates the appraisal as managers adjust gross-profit and inventory-turn objectives, while accounting for the costs associated with holding a vehicle.
Another product, the Predictive Market Report, forecasts wholesale values instead of relying exclusively on historical auction results.
VINCUE also disclosed early performance information from the first 100 dealerships using Buy Center Pro for Service Lane Acquisition. During the first nine months of 2026, those dealers generated an additional $5 million in front-end gross profit from service-lane acquisitions, according to the company.
Buy Center Pro includes an AI agent called Benjamin. VINCUE has also announced more than 20 partner integrations involving companies such as Tekion, DriveCentric, LumaScanner, AppraisalPRO, and Auto Hauler Exchange.
Wavecrest Executives Join The Board
As part of the financing, Wavecrest Managing Partner Deepak Sindwani and Principal Anthony Giannobile joined VINCUE’s board of directors.
They will advise the leadership team on strategy, operating scale, and potential partnerships involving other companies in Wavecrest’s portfolio.
FM Capital also increased its investment in VINCUE. The transportation-focused venture firm typically backs early- and growth-stage companies and draws its investor base from automotive dealers, manufacturers, suppliers, distributors, and insurers.
TD Securities served as VINCUE’s financial adviser. Kennyhertz Perry Attorneys at Law and Hogan Lovells Cadwalader advised VINCUE, while Gunderson Dettmer represented Wavecrest.

Insider Brief
Promise Robotics has raised CAN$40 million in Series B funding to expand its network of automated homebuilding production facilities across North America.
Led by White Star Capital, with participation from Horizons Ventures, Radical Ventures and PSP Investments, the funding will support expansion of the company’s Factory-as-a-Service platform.

Promise Robotics has raised CAN$40 million in Series B funding to expand its network of automated production facilities for homebuilders across North America.
White Star Capital led the round, with participation from Horizons Ventures , Radical Ventures and Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments), according to the company . The funding will go to expanding its production network, allowing more builders to access robotic manufacturing without developing and operating their own factories.
Promise’s Factory-as-a-Service platform takes existing home designs and converts them into a coordinated process covering robotic manufacturing, factory operations and installation at construction sites. The company said the system is designed to shorten construction schedules and increase production capacity while reducing builders’ dependence on skilled construction labor.
“Homebuilding can’t scale on trade labor alone, and builders shouldn’t have to become manufacturers to grow. We’re building the production infrastructure the industry can scale on; a network of intelligent factories that get better with every home it helps build,” said co-founder and CEO Ramtin Attar. “This round lets us extend that network across North America.”
The announcement follows a multi-year commercial agreement with D.R. Horton , the largest U.S. homebuilder by volume. According to Promise Robotics, D.R. Horton is the first major U.S. homebuilder to adopt its Factory-as-a-Service platform.
Promise Robotics, which has spent six years developing its technology and business model, operates production facilities in Calgary and Nisku, Canada, and plans to open its first U.S. facility in Phoenix, Arizona. The company reported more than 2,500 housing units under contract across three markets.

O15 Capital Supports 11th St. Workshop Acquisition With $23.6 Million Facility
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:26 PM
O15 Capital Supports 11th St. Workshop Acquisition With $23.6 Million Facility
O15 Capital Partners has provided debt and equity financing supporting Bluestone Equity Partners’ acquisition of 11th St. Workshop.
Through its Emerging America Credit Opportunities fund, O15 supplied a senior secured last-out term loan as part of a $23.6 million unitranche facility. The firm also made an equity co-investment.
The transaction provides additional detail about the financing behind Bluestone’s acquisition of a majority stake in 11th St. Workshop, which designs and fabricates physical environments for brand activations, events, and other experiential projects.
Flexible Capital For A Lower-Middle-Market Acquisition
A unitranche facility combines senior and subordinated debt into a single financing structure for the borrower. Within that arrangement, a last-out lender generally agrees to receive repayment after first-out lenders under the terms of an intercreditor agreement.
This structure can simplify a company’s debt package while allowing different capital providers to assume distinct levels of risk.
O15’s equity co-investment also gives the firm ownership exposure alongside its credit position.
The investment reflects O15’s strategy of partnering with established private equity sponsors and providing flexible capital to lower-middle-market businesses.
Financial terms beyond the $23.6 million facility were not disclosed.
Supporting 11th Street’s National Expansion
11th St. Workshop works with agencies and brands to design, manufacture, and install complex physical environments.
Bluestone plans to invest in additional production capacity and services while expanding the company’s presence in sports, entertainment, and experiential marketing.
11th Street has begun increasing capacity at its Los Angeles facility and intends to build a broader national platform.
The financing from O15 will support the acquisition and provide a capital structure for that next growth phase.
Bluestone specializes in sports, media, and entertainment investments. O15 focuses on growth capital for lower-middle-market businesses and underserved communities across healthcare, education, and business services.
The parties did not disclose the unitranche facility’s interest rate, maturity date, repayment schedule, leverage ratio, or the size of O15’s equity co-investment.

The $6.3 Billion Breach at Binance (October 2026): A threat actor, whom the FBI has identified as North Korea's TraderTraitor group, compromised a developer's laptop to access an internal service container with the permissions to initiate withdrawal requests. Using that access as a starting point, the attackers exploited additional points of compromise and an Ethereum account-delegation mechanism to gain transaction approval authority over a hot wallet . In around 20 minutes, the threat actors drained billions of dollars in assets.
Claude Code Extension Tampering (October 2026): A tampered copy of the Claude Code extension was served on the Cursor Extension Marketplace for several hours to deploy a persistent SSH backdoor.

"10% of households drive almost 50% of US consumer spending. For the business of hospitality or fandom, the stakes have never been higher: you have to truly know your customer. SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sequel.io , a video-driven audience intelligence and activation platform, today announced $15 million in funding led by Sorenson Capital, bringing total funding to approximately $26 million. New investors in the round include High Alpha, Album VC and Webflow Ventures, with additional participation from existing investors Javelin Venture Partners, Struck Capital, Alumni Ventures and Social Leverage. The investment will support product innovation and enterprise growth as Sequel helps marketers turn human video engagement and website behavior into unique first-party intelligence that AI agents can act on across GTM.
From Human Engagement to First-Party Audience Intelligence

Sequel takes a different approach. Its video is hosted directly on a brand's website and connects what people watch, ask and respond to during live, simulive and on-demand video with the other content they explore across the site. It's the only provider in its category combining these signals at both the individual contact and account level. This gives marketers a clearer view of audience interests, emerging purchase intent and engagement across buying groups, and the context to make outreach and experiences more relevant.
"Video on its own can't build buyer trust at scale, and AI on its own can't create the context brands need to grow pipeline," said Oana Manolache , co-founder and CEO of Sequel.io. Branded egg company Henfruit has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Lok Capital, DSG Consumer Partners and RPSG Capital Ventures, its first external investment since it was set up in 2014.

Henfruit will use the capital to expand its presence across India, strengthen its production capabilities and scale its supply chain. It also plans to widen its online and offline distribution network.
Founded by Tarun Gupta, Henfruit operated as a bootstrapped business for over a decade before securing this funding. The company sells packaged and graded eggs, focusing on traceability and testing in a market where most eggs are still sold loose and unbranded.
Henfruit conducts daily egg testing at its in-house laboratory and independent third-party labs, with test reports made publicly available to consumers. The tests cover antibiotics, banned drugs and freshness, while the eggs undergo a six-stage cleaning and UV sanitation process before being packed. The grading process is automated.
Henfruit offers three product lines, Protein Max, Farm White and Power Brown and provides consumers with a direct phone number to contact its founder.
It currently processes more than four crore eggs a month and serves consumers in 15 major cities, with a workforce of more than 300 people. The company said its scale has grown about 10 times over the past three years, and it expects revenue to cross Rs 350 crore in FY27.
Four crore eggs a month works out to roughly 48 crore eggs a year, or about 0.3% of the eggs India produces annually.
Henfruit competes with Gurugram-based Eggoz, which follows an asset-light model, sourcing eggs from local poultry farmers and supplying them through its own distribution network.
Eggoz has raised over $32 million to date. Its largest round was $20 million led by Gaja Capital in June 2025, following an $8.8 million Series B led by IvyCap Ventures in December 2022.
India is the world's second-largest egg producer. It produced an estimated 149.11 billion eggs in 2024-25, up 4.44% from the previous year, according to the Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025 released by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
Commercial poultry farms accounted for about 84.5% of that output, with the rest coming from backyard and semi-commercial farming. Per capita availability rose to 106 eggs a year in 2024-25, from 62 eggs a decade earlier in 2014-15.
Production is concentrated in the south and east. Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, West Bengal and Karnataka together contribute about 64.37% of the country's eggs.

By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:07 AM
Darcy Geothermal Raises $15 Million To Expand Commercial Heating And Cooling
Darcy Geothermal has raised approximately $15 million in Series B funding to expand its commercial geothermal heating and cooling operations across the United States. Aligned Climate Capital and Büetigen co-led the round.
Darcy plans to use the funding to expand geographically, hire additional employees, continue developing geological analysis and energy-modeling software, and advance its proprietary geothermal technologies.
The company will also use the capital to commercialize its Geothermal-as-a-Service offering, which combines project financing, design, installation, operation, and ongoing service through a single contract and fixed monthly fee.
Reducing The Upfront Cost Of Geothermal Projects
Commercial geothermal systems can reduce heating and cooling expenses, but projects often require substantial upfront capital and specialized geological, engineering, financial, and construction expertise.
Darcy’s service model is intended to simplify that process. For qualified customers, the company provides geothermal assessment, system design, financing, construction, operation, and long-term service.
The structure gives building owners an alternative to paying the project’s full cost in advance. It also moves responsibility for processing the federal investment tax credit from the customer to Darcy’s project model.
Federal tax incentives remain available for commercial geothermal heat-pump projects following the accelerated phaseout of certain wind and solar credits.
Darcy expects this structure to make geothermal systems accessible to more building owners by reducing financial and administrative barriers.
Groundwater-Based Technology Requires Fewer Wells
Darcy develops geothermal systems that use groundwater to move heat into and out of buildings.
Its proprietary heat-exchange approach is designed to produce greater thermal capacity while using fewer wells and less land than many conventional geothermal configurations. That can make the technology suitable for dense urban sites, existing buildings, and other locations where drilling space is limited.
The company has built or contracted more than 80 geothermal projects involving over 235 dipole wells. Its internal geology team has completed more than 2,000 project evaluations covering different property types and locations.
Customers include commercial real estate owners, schools, healthcare organizations, government agencies, data centers, and operators of other large buildings or campuses.
Darcy has established operations in the Midwest and secured projects in the Northeast, Mountain West, and Pacific Northwest. It has also formed eight sales-representative partnerships covering 17 states.
The company is considering a future presence in Canada and the European Union.
Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems account for a substantial share of building energy consumption. Darcy is positioning its technology as a way for commercial property owners to address rising energy costs while adopting an alternative to conventional heating and cooling.
KEY QUOTES:
Geothermal has tremendous potential to help building owners lower their energy costs, but the complexity of developing and financing these projects has kept many from moving forward. We’ve spent years building the technical expertise and project delivery capabilities to address those challenges. This investment will allow us to bring that experience to more markets and give customers a simpler way to move from evaluating geothermal to putting a system in the ground.
Andrew Steiner, CEO of Darcy Geothermal
Heating and cooling are among the largest energy costs in any commercial building, and electricity prices aren’t coming down. Darcy gives owners of large buildings and campuses a lower-cost, high-reliability alternative, and its integrated model, from design through long-term operations, is why we’re confident this capital will translate into projects getting built. This is a team that has executed for years, with a growing multi-state backlog to show for it.
Peter Davidson, CEO of Aligned Climate Capital

candidates.title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked
candidates.snippet: Citi is the latest major financial institution to put the breaks on personal finance AI agents.
candidates.text:
Citibank, the third largest commercial bank in the United States, changed its terms of service this week, telling customers who use third-party AI tools for personal finance that anything that goes wrong is their problem — even if they get hacked.
AI agents, ranging from frontier lab models to purpose-built personal finance tools, can be given the credentials to your bank account and other online financial portals, with the idea that they can analyze spending and investment decisions, offer advice, and even handle transactions and bill payments.
But financial institutions aren’t thrilled with the unreliable AI actors in their systems, and are telling customers that they won’t be held responsible for reversing an intentional or unintentional transaction made by automated assistants.
“As third-party AI tools become more widely available, we want customers to understand the risks associated with sharing banking credentials or authorizing those tools to access their accounts,” a Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch. “We recently updated our Online User Agreement to provide greater clarity about those risks and to reinforce that customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents.”
JPMorgan and Bank of America , the two largest banks in the country, announced similar policies last month. And PNC, the eighth largest bank, changed its terms today.
Citi’s update goes beyond telling customers that they are responsible for anything their agents may do; it also informs them that if the AI tool leaks their credentials or is hacked, the customer will be responsible for anything hackers do with their account. Banking giant Citizens similarly emailed its customers this week, warning that they are also on the hook for anything their AI assistant does, according to an email seen by TechCrunch.
As AI startups look for more revenue, breaking into personal finance presents an attractive opportunity for companies to add value for customers and wet their beaks in the stream of fees generated by the sector. But if consumers are already leery of sharing their email or chat records with an AI agent, bank and brokerage accounts offer a new trust challenge.
Anthropic’s approach is telling: The personal finance tool it launched earlier this month is explicitly billed as “read-only” and “can’t move, manage, or invest your money.”
Beyond cybersecurity concerns, banks also view efforts to enter their franchise as a competitive threat. Markets shuddered briefly in reaction to the prospect of AI tools making it easier for consumers to avoid unnecessary fees or low-interest deposit accounts that pad bank margins. But if AI agents become an important way to interact with financial decisions, banks will fight to control that pathway. Citi’s terms note that AI agents it provides can be used by customers without worrying about additional liability.
The reaction by banks is part of a broader trend among businesses of all stripes: AI labs promise that their agents will revolutionize the way people engage with a variety of service providers, then the service providers say “hold on a minute.” We’ve seen it in everything from car-hailing to food service , and how these relationships play out will help determine which AI investments pay off.
